rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The limbs expose every misdeed, including the slander and evil people spread, despite their efforts to conceal it now.
rows.anchor: no misdeed of theirs can remain hidden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the phrase about that day, dīn means retribution.
rows.anchor: The word دﻳۡﻦٌ in ﻳَﻮۡﻣَmeans “retribution.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because facts remain hidden today, people misunderstand God and fail to grasp that He will establish truth and eliminate evil.
rows.anchor: Today many things are hidden, as a result of which these people have many misconceptions about God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day they will recognize God as truth and justice and as the One who unveils every fact.
rows.anchor: God is a personification of truth and justice and at the same time One Who unveils all facts.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world's mixture of truth and falsehood will end when people are sorted by faith and morality, as in the Qur'anic image of souls being paired.
rows.anchor: the truth is hidden and pebbles and pearls are intermixed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day, good men and women will be grouped with their counterparts, as will evil men and women.
rows.anchor: good men and good women, and evil men and evil women will be grouped together.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good will be acquitted of false accusations and receive forgiveness and honourable provision, which together encompass the Hereafter's favours.
rows.anchor: the good ones will be totally acquitted of the nonesical things being hatched against them and for them will be forgiveness and an honourable sustenance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 27–34 prevent social disorder that leads to lustful looks, accusations, and sexual misconduct.
rows.anchor: In these verses, directives are given to prevent disorder in the society that leads to lustful stares, accusations and moral misconduct.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage first restricts the pre-Islamic freedom to visit other people's homes.
rows.anchor: first of all certain restrictions are imposed on the freedom that existed in pre-Islamic jāhiliyyah society regarding visiting one another in houses.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Widows and able-minded, able-bodied slaves should be married so wrongdoers cannot spread evil.
rows.anchor: slaves must be married off so that the miscreants are not able to spread evil.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mukātaba law and financial aid should help slaves gain free status and raise their moral standard through faith and harmony.
rows.anchor: the generous law of mukatābat has been revealed and people are urged to financially help the slaves so that they too have the status of free of individuals, their moral standard is raised

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents are trapped in confusion and vent their frenzy by saying whatever comes to mind.
rows.anchor: These people are not able to find a way out from their imbroglio and utter whatever comes to their mind.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deliberately denying a truth is senseless, and these objections display that same attitude.
rows.anchor: when a person deliberately denies something true, he displays a senseless attitude – the very one found in these objections.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This section sets out the objections, their motives and consequences, adds further objections, and urges the Prophet and companions to ignore them patiently.
rows.anchor: In this section, the afore-mentioned objections are cited, their motives are highlighted and the consequence of this blind animosity is also depicted.

none: English translation of verses only; no commentary point is stated.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response begins with the same word as the objections, and answers first the last objection raised in verse 8.
rows.anchor: The last of the objections cited in verse 8 is answered the foremost.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can give the Prophet better worldly gifts, and will give them one day, but this world is a trial rather than a reward.
rows.anchor: God can give all these things to the Prophet (sws) and in fact will do one day.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both scarcity and abundance test people; lasting success belongs to those who fear God and succeed in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: This world is not a place of reward; it is a place of trial. Scarcity and abundance are both forms of trial.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denial of the Hereafter leads them to mistake worldly success for proof that they are rightly guided.
rows.anchor: they regard their success in this world to be a proof of being on the right path

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They know God has prepared Hell for those who deny the Hereafter despite the extent of their worldly lands and orchards.
rows.anchor: They very well know God has prepared Hell

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell's rage and roar express its anger and desire for revenge, as it roars like a lion at the wrongdoers from afar.
rows.anchor: It will rage with anger to seek revenge from them and roar like a lion when it sees them from afar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrow, fettered punishment recalls the sealed enclosure and high columns described in Sūrah al-Humazah; chains are mentioned elsewhere too.
rows.anchor: they will be enshrouded in it, fastened to columns very high

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thubūr means death and destruction; death is the escape they desire, but it will be withheld from them.
rows.anchor: The word ﺛ%ﺒ%ﻮۡر means “death and destruction.” Death would be the only option these people would think of

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elsewhere their condition is described as neither living nor dying, with death attacking them from every side.
rows.anchor: they will neither live nor die.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They face one calamity after another and call for death repeatedly, but to no avail.
rows.anchor: today they will face one calamity after the other and will call for death after each of them but to no avail.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call for many deaths may be spoken literally by Hell's keepers or may portray the situation.
rows.anchor: These words can be uttered literally from the keepers of Hell or could be a portrayal of the situation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of Hell is meant to confront people who cannot see beyond worldly life with their final outcome.
rows.anchor: These verses mention the real purpose for which all these details of Hell have been mentioned.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly wealth makes the opponents arrogant and contemptuous of poor believers; awareness of the Hereafter would make them envy the believers and lament their own fate.
rows.anchor: because of their palaces and orchards and mock at the believers for their indigence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their worldly riches blind them to the Hereafter and prevent them from seeing beyond themselves.
rows.anchor: arrogance of their worldly riches has blinded them and they are not able to see beyond their own selves.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise is given to believers as a reward for deeds they deserve.
rows.anchor: God will assure them that they have achieved it because of their deeds and that they fully deserve it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise is the believers' eternal abode, from which they will not fear being removed.
rows.anchor: They will not have the fear of being deprived from it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Paradise, believers will receive whatever they desire and continue to receive it.
rows.anchor: they will get in it and continue to do so whatever they desire.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has made a certain promise of Paradise to believers and is responsible for fulfilling it.
rows.anchor: God has made a certain promise of giving it to the believers and it is obligatory upon Him to fulfil this promise.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deities named earlier in verses 2–3 had made the idolaters indifferent to the Hereafter and led them to mock the Qur'an and Messenger.
rows.anchor: Mentioned earlier in verses 2-3 are the deities the Idolaters associated with God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters treated the next world as a bluff, or assumed worldly success meant they would succeed there too.
rows.anchor: they will succeed because they are leading such a successful life in this world.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dialogue's answer comes from angels and righteous people who were actually worshipped.
rows.anchor: from the angels and the righteous who were actually worshipped.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alleged deities without real existence are gathered but do not join the dialogue.
rows.anchor: they will not be part of the conversation since they never existed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elsewhere idols are consigned to Hell alongside their worshippers, making their fate clear to them.
rows.anchor: these idols will be consigned to Hell together with their worshippers so that their fate becomes evident to them.
